reviews.review:
Highly recommended for Warhammer/sci-fi/FPS fans.

I found the single player story quite enjoyable and full of action with fun and challenging foes to eradicate in the name of the Emperor. It's very straightforward without character-defining choices, but rather a good awe-some and cinematic experience over, through, and under the Forge World Graia. Superb voice acting and solid graphics that show off spectacular scenes throughout.

The multiplayer suffers from no dedicated server capability and most game modes are dead these days, though you shouldn't find yourself waiting for a simple Seize Ground match. Other than the lack of server consistency, I enjoyed levelling up and unlocking the customization options and equipment. The level of detail you can utilize to create a unique looking character (or uniformity to canonical chapters/legions) is deep enough to spend plenty of time trying out new schemes.
If you liked Gears of War you will love this game.

Play as Captain Titus in this gory third-person-shooter version of the 40k universe (with pretty much no racial/chapter diversity), a battle-hardened Ultramarine who has no idea how to jump over 2-foot ledges or direct instructions. Although some of the game's functions may not work as well as the devs might've hoped, it still delivers hardcore killing-action without any delay (sometimes it gets annoying, but what can you do? Stop crying). Surprisingly similar melee weapons give you many opportunities to pulverise, slash and pound your enemies with; so you'll certainly have your fair share of blood and gore (or don't, and just hoard ammo,  let your squad walk in first and be the kind of captain that says: "Screw glory, I'm gonna hang back and pick everything off with a pistol"). And even when you finish the campaign (Which is a challenging go-here-and-hit-these-things type story on it's own) you can go head to head with the other 4 or 5 players that still play the multiplayer feature, or form a team with up to 3 other players and take on 21 repetitive waves of overpowered enemies in the slightly more popular and less broken exterminatus mode. If you're the sort of person that wants a FPS version of DoW, this is it.
Note: Hard mode is pretty easy

Here's my original, lazy, grumpy, and brief review of this game from 12/22/2013:
"Decent story, boring gameplay. I was tired with the gameplay in under an hour and just wanted the game to end. I completed it after forcing myself to finish it, but I'm never playing it again. I wouldn't recommend this game unless you've got a hard-on for the Warhammer setting."

Well, I played Dawn of War for the first time, found myself intrigued by 40K, studied a little bit about the lore, have been getting interested in other 40K video games, and I came back to Space Marine to play it again, despite specifically saying I'd never play it again, because my new interest in 40K basically required it.

Knowing all that I know now from playing Dawn of War to completion, dipping into its expansions, playing a bit of Dawn of War II, and reading bunches of forum posts about 40K and wikis about 40K, Space Marine made so much more sense to me this time around. There's quite a bit of 40K atmosphere in Space Marine, but without context or understanding, much of it won't "click" with players. My first time through the game, when I was completely 40K ignorant, I didn't know what Chaos was, why people talked like it was the Crusades, who or what the Emperor was, what a Space Marine was, what Chaos gods are, just how extreme exterminatus is, what "waaagh!" is, and much, much more. 

While I'm sure some fans of the franchise may have had their interest kicked of with Space Marine, it didn't do it for me. Dawn of War is what taught me enough to get me on board and it's where I had the jaw-dropping epiphany that it's fantasy...just done in space with fancy tech. When I finally realized that, it's when most everything started to really fall into place for me and I quickly began to like the franchise. With Space Marine, however, I just never caught on and none of the lore stuck with me.

So here's the thing, though: my original review is still fairly accurate of my feelings about the game. The only difference is that I loved the look of the game and enjoyed the lore so much more because I knew what was going on. In other words, having some beginner level knowledge of 40K drastically increased my enjoyment of the game. In fact, after an hour, I wasn't bored this time. Now, after about 5 hours or so, that's when I finally got bored, and the last few hours were a drag. Like I said, my original review is still fairly accurate of my feelings. The combat is very simple and got stale for me fast.

For me, the worst thing about the combat was some clunkiness in the melee, but mostly poorly balanced weapon options. The melta gun and lascannon are infinitely better than pretty much everything else. I really liked the bolter, too, but you always have that a little bit into the game. The choices of your third and fourth weapon slot fillers are either amazing guns or pretty lame guns. I like "the best gun for the job" more than "the best gun," and I did not like every gun you could equip instead of the lascannon and melta gun. They seemed drastically inferior to these weapons.

I still had to force myself to finish the game, because within a few hours of the end, I was ready to be done, as the gameplay had ceased to entertain me and I just wanted to be done with the game again. I will admit that knowledge of 40K lore significantly increased my interest and enjoyment in the game, making me eager to learn and experience more of the setting. That said, I could've learned a lot more by flippantly following 40K wiki links for 8 hours instead. I'm glad this game gave me some more perspective into Space Marines and a bit of the interactions between them, Imperial Guard, and Inquisitors, but that's about it. The actual gameplay was just a drag after a little while for me.
Buy it and come help us purge some fallen battle brothers.
